plain_summary: Review a cholinesterase inhibitor with a listed systemic anticholinergic at age 65 or older.

medicine_groups.name: Anticholinergics listed in STOPP-M1 or STOPP-D14
medicine_groups.note: Use the named ingredients in either local list. Benztropine is also called benzatropine, chlorpheniramine is also called chlorphenamine, and dosulepin is also called dothiepin. Check the active ingredient of non-prescription products. Benzhexol is another name for trihexyphenidyl. For chlorphenamine and tizanidine, check the ingredient if the brand is unfamiliar.

rule_for_models: At age 65 or older, cite both medicines when donepezil, galantamine or rivastigmine and a systemic anticholinergic in Group B share treatment days based on the supply dates, quantities and units used per day or patch replacement intervals, whatever the anticholinergic is used for. Include systemic patches such as rivastigmine and oxybutynin, exclude local-only creams, eye drops, nasal sprays, inhalers and completed switches with no overlap, and do not calculate a numerical burden score. For plausible overlap at age 65 or older or with age unknown, cite both medicines as a possible finding only if age is unknown or directions are unclear or as needed, confirm whether the person is at least 65 if age is missing, and ask about actual use, including products bought without prescription, and any worsening of memory or confusion.
cannot_be_seen: Dispensing does not establish actual use, indication or a prescriber’s intent. Treatment and assessments elsewhere may be missing.
ask_the_gp: Could you review concurrent use of the cholinesterase inhibitor and systemic anticholinergic, and whether an alternative with fewer anticholinergic effects would suit this patient?
